blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: High-resolution generation enables video world models to render fine-grained scene structures and textures, but directly generating high-resolution video incurs substantial computational and memory costs. We present ScaleWorld, a causal video model that unifies low-resolution world prediction and high-resolution refinement within a single shared backbone. By refining its own predictions, ScaleWorld produces high-resolution world videos without requiring a separate refinement model. For each video chunk, the shared backbone first completes a low-resolution prediction and then performs one-step high-resolution refinement conditioned on that prediction. To support efficient streaming generation, we maintain separate causal states with a long low-resolution history for prediction and a short high-resolution history for refinement. To address task interference during distillation, we separate specialist optimization from capability consolidation and introduce task-asymmetric on-policy distillation (TA-OPD). This procedure transfers prediction and refinement behaviors from specialized teachers into a shared student through local velocity matching under their respective sampling and history policies. {Extensive experiments demonstrate that ScaleWorld achieves high-quality world generation with improved computational and memory efficiency.

blocks.en:
Video world models generate evolving visual environments conditioned on
observations and control inputs [ 20 , 3 , 18 ] .
High-resolution generation enables these models to depict fine-grained
scene structures and textures as the environment evolves.
Causal video diffusion supports incremental generation [ 27 , 9 ] , but directly generating
high-resolution video incurs substantial computational and memory costs.
Increasing spatial resolution raises both denoising computation and
temporal-state storage, making high-resolution output costly to sustain
in streaming world generation.

blocks.en:
We present ScaleWorld , a shared causal model for streaming world
prediction and streaming high-resolution refinement.
Both roles follow a chunk-wise autoregressive paradigm: the model first
completes a low-resolution (LR) prediction, then uses the same backbone
to perform one-step high-resolution (HR) refinement conditioned on that
prediction and its own refinement history.
No future LR chunks are required, so each completed prediction can be
refined without waiting for a full video.
The native LR output remains independently usable, and HR outputs do not
feed back into prediction history.
This design must accommodate the roles’ distinct temporal requirements
while consolidating both capabilities in shared parameters.

blocks.en:
To support efficient inference, we share model weights while maintaining
separate causal states.
World prediction retains a longer clean history at low resolution to
infer scene evolution.
Refinement already receives the current LR structure, content, and motion,
and uses a shorter HR history to support the continuity of synthesized detail.
It further retains key–value (KV) states from the denoising forward pass
as noisy-forward history , avoiding an additional HR model evaluation
for history construction.
These asymmetric histories limit the cost of refinement while preserving
longer temporal context for world prediction.

blocks.en:
Sharing visual representations does not ensure that prediction and
refinement can be effectively distilled together.
In our joint distillation experiments, we observe conflicting gradients
between the two tasks, and better reconstruction during refinement can accompany
reduced temporal stability in world prediction
(Appendix C.1 ).
We therefore separate specialist optimization from capability consolidation.
Starting from a jointly trained and causally adapted model, we first
optimize prediction and refinement specialists under their respective
sampling and history policies.
Building on on-policy distillation [ 14 , 31 ] ,
we introduce task-asymmetric on-policy distillation (TA-OPD) to
consolidate the frozen specialists into a shared student.
TA-OPD matches expert velocities at student-visited denoising queries for
prediction, and at matched conditional noise queries with network-specific
recurrent histories for refinement, respecting the roles’ different execution policies.

We evaluate ScaleWorld on camera-controlled world generation, examining
native prediction retention, refinement of fixed generated inputs, and
complete HR generation.
The shared model retains competitive native prediction performance and
achieves HR generation quality comparable to a separate specialist cascade.
Matched deployments of the same unified checkpoint show that sharing
weights reduces peak GPU memory while preserving throughput.
Noisy-forward history accelerates refinement over clean recommit
by avoiding an extra HR forward pass.

backbone while retaining an independently usable native prediction path. • A training and inference framework combining TA-OPD and asymmetric

quality, with controlled deployment measurements of memory savings

consolidate separately optimized prediction and refinement behaviors into

specialist velocities at the student’s current queries under each task’s
sampling and memory policies.

At inference, the shared model alternates between prediction and
refinement. Each completed LR chunk updates the clean prediction memory
and conditions its HR counterpart; the refinement forward simultaneously
produces the HR output and the noisy-forward KV for subsequent chunks.
This process uses only the available LR prefix and follows the same
causal-memory rules as training. With fixed parameters, independent
sampling streams, and unchanged prediction settings, enabling refinement
leaves the native LR sample path unchanged.

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en:
We presented ScaleWorld , a shared causal model for camera-controlled
prediction and high-resolution refinement. Its asymmetric temporal
contexts allocate long history to low-resolution prediction, while
specialist training and TA-OPD integrate the two capabilities.
Experiments show comparable overall generation quality to a separate
specialist cascade, retained native prediction capability, and lower
resident deployment memory. The resulting model produces high-resolution worlds
incrementally with one backbone. Limitations are discussed in
Appendix E .

blocks.en:

blocks.en: Appendix E Limitations
blocks.zh: 附录E 限制

blocks.en:
Our formulation targets camera-controlled visual prediction,
not an explicit physical state simulator.
High-resolution refinement may introduce unsupported structures
or alter appearance even when it does not feed back into the
native prediction recurrence.
Although refinement training incorporates synthetic degradations
designed to mimic generation artifacts [ 8 , 34 ] ,
these degradations may not fully capture the errors in world-model
predictions. A residual gap between training conditions and generated
LR inputs may therefore remain, potentially limiting refinement
robustness during self-cascading.
Capability retention and temporal robustness must therefore
be interpreted within the evaluated controls, domains, and horizons.
